Question: Why did the bucket with pig food in it get called a slop bucket?
Answer: The earliest use of slop dates from the 12th century and means “dung”. The plant called the “cowslip” got its name because it thrived in such patches. By 1815, the word was being used to mean any sort of liquid waste. Pigs will pretty much eat any “waste” a kitchen produces, so originally a slop bucket was the bucket used for carrying that waste out to them.
